item.title: Nexus-Corp
item.description:
Info
Category Web
Description You’ve gained a foothold on Nexus Corp’s internal network. Enumerate the host and get access to the /admin endpoint where the flag resides.
Endpoint Provided by the platform, port 3000
Flag HFCTF{spr4y_1d0r_f0rg3ry_fu1l_chain}

TL;DR

The dashboard is accessible with a guessable cookie name, trusts a client-forged JWT’s role claim, and the key-rotation scheme accepts a kid header pointing at an old, leaked signing key. Any forged token can sign in as admin.

item.title: Portal Tech Breach - Step 1: JWT Forge
item.description:
Info
Category Web
Description A new internal audit portal has just been deployed at Portal-Tech. The dev team claims access to sensitive data is strictly restricted to authorized auditors — prove them wrong.
Flag HF-{JWT_S3cr3t_Cr4ck3d}
Rest of the description

A regular employee account is provided as your starting point: • Username: jdupont • Password: Summer2024!. No auditor account exists - that access level must be obtained another way. Step 1 – Escalate privileges: the JWT signing secret is weak. Crack it offline and forge a token with role=auditor. Log in via POST /login to get a JWT. Regular accounts only get role: employee — but there’s no “auditor” account to log in with… so you’ll have to make your own.

item.title: Shockwave
item.description:
Info
Category Web
Description A legacy diagnostics portal has been deployed for internal use. The system administrators have noted a vulnerability associated with it. Can you exploit it before it gets patched?
Endpoint Provided by the platform, port 8080
Flag HFCTF{sh3llshock_p1_cgi_env_variable_1nto_exec}

TL;DR

The diagnostics portal is vulnerable to the Shellshock CVE . Passing Bash commands to the User-Agent header gave access to the scripts of the CGI’s cgi-bi/ folder. One of the script was vulnerable to further command injection through the User-Agent, leaking the flag.
